Advocate

Order No.03 / Dated : 05.12.2025 I.A. No.7504 of 2025 Heard learned counsel on behalf of appellant in I.A. No.7504 of 2025 which has been filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay of 1571 days in preferring the instant appeal.

The appellant is owner of the offending vehicle and the appeal is preferred against the judgment and award of compensation passed in Motor Accident Claim Case No.96/2016, whereby and whereunder the compensation of Rs.75,62,225/- has been awarded in favour of the claimants against the Insurance Company, with a right of recovery from the owner of the vehicle, on the ground that there was a fundamental breach of terms of insurance policy as the driver was not holding valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.
On the point of limitation, it is submitted that owner had appeared before the learned Tribunal and contested the claim and filed the written statement.

In an analogous case arising from the same accident, compensation was awarded to the claimants in Motor Accident Claim Case No.92/2016,
wherein total liability was fixed on the Insurance Company without any right of recovery having been granted in its favour.

In this view of matter, since the vehicle was insured and the driver was having license, therefore, the appellant was under the impression that liability to pay compensation was on Insurance Company,
and no right of recovery was granted.
However, later on, when certificate proceeding was initiated against the appellant, then he came to know about the right of recovery having been granted in favour of the Insurance Company.

sentences.text:
Mr. Ashutosh Anand, learned counsel appearing on behalf of Insurance Company submits that there is an inordinate delay of nearly five years and since he was in appearance before this Court,
therefore, the plea that he was ignorant about the result and final outcome of the case, is not tenable.

Having considered the submissions advanced on behalf of both sides and taking into account the fact that in a claim case arising out of the same accident, no such right of recovery was granted in favour of the Insurance Company against the appellant, therefore, there appears to be some force in the argument that the appellant was under a wrong impression that no adverse order has been passed in the said motor accident claim case against him.
Under the circumstance, delay in filing the appeal is condoned and I.A. No.7504 of 2025 is allowed.

Certificate proceeding against the appellant in connection with Execution (Recovery) Case No.36 of 2025 pending in the Court of learned District Judge IV-cum-Motor Accident Claim Tribunal,
Dhanbad, is stayed till further order.
